Constructor initializer

resharper_align_multiline_ctor_init #

Align a wrapped constructor initializer with the first argument. Not read by the C# formatter: measured one key away from the export on a probe carrying a : base(…) and a : this(…) whose argument lists both chop under the 120-column margin, and false returns it byte-identical — the arguments stay on the continuation indent rather than on the first argument's column, which is what the export's own true should have produced. Two negative controls on the same probe: resharper_csharp_align_first_arg_by_paren = true and resharper_csharp_indent_invocation_pars = outside both move that initializer's arguments.

Typetrue / false
Defaulttrue
Default known fromthe Rider export, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two
TierD — recorded so the key is not reported unknown; nothing reads it yet

resharper_wrap_ctor_initializer_style #

The constructor initializer's wrap style, in the language-generic spelling the export writes. ⚠ Probed rather than reasoned about: eleven fixtures under this repository's own .editorconfig, one cleanupcode invocation per configuration, each fixture first shown to move under the key that really governs its construct. Inert at all three values on a : this(…) that overflows, at 120 and at 60 columns, and with csharp_place_constructor_initializer_on_same_line = false in the same run — byte-identical to that run without this key. That placement key is what moves a constructor initializer onto its own line.

Typeone of wrap_if_long, chop_if_long, chop_always
